speech_en: Tiny me — my whole instruction book was the very first ever fully read!
speech_de: Winzig, ich — mein ganzer Bauplan war der allererste, der je komplett gelesen wurde!
scenario: The tiniest, simplest member of the set: a small, perfectly ROUND ball-shaped phage character (not elongated, not tall) with big happy eyes, studded all around its edge with small blunt rounded bumps — not legs, not spikes, not a starburst. Unlike T4's landing legs and T7's leg-stubs, THIS CHARACTER HAS NO LEGS OR TAIL OF ANY KIND (the key visual difference from its cousins' coloring pages) — it simply floats and rests directly against the giant bacterium-planet character, touching it with two or three of its rounded edge-bumps, and hands over a tiny rolled scroll (its whole tiny instruction book, referencing the 'first genome ever read' story) toward a plain round porthole/hatch emblem on the bacterium's side. No fight, no bursting — mirrors the set's 'show the friendly mechanism, not menace' convention and reuses the t4/t7-bacteriophage precedent of turning the docking structure into blunt rounded studs to avoid a starburst, the single riskiest failure mode named in SKILL.md for anything radiating from a hub.
status: DONE — rendered on gemini-3-pro-image. 4 API render attempts (1-4), none of which is the final artwork used: attempt 1 drew the bacterium's hatch as a SEPARATE small character with its own face holding the scroll (confusing 'who is E. coli' narrative) and had zero left-edge bleed; attempt 2 fixed the composition (single phage + single bacterium, hatch correctly a plain doorway with no face, excellent 3-edge bleed: top 0.144/left 0.138/right 0.073/bottom 0.050 on the raw PNG) but filled the hatch AND the bacterium's mouth solid black, violating the 'no solid fills except pupils' rule; attempts 3 and 4 (revised prompts explicitly forbidding the black fill, then reframing it positively as a flat outline 'coin/badge') traded that defect for a WORSE one each time (attempt 3 kept the black hatch fill AND regressed left-edge bleed to 0.0; attempt 4 removed the black fill but regressed left-edge bleed to 0.0 again and degraded the phage's bump-studding). Per SKILL.md's 'crop, don't re-roll' principle (applied here to a solid-fill defect rather than a border), attempt 2 — the best-composed, best-bled raw render — was kept as the base and patched deterministically with NO further API call: a morphological opening (17x17 structuring element: erode then reconstruct via dilation intersected with the original ink mask) isolated the two solid-black regions (the hatch disc, ~11.6k px, and the bacterium's filled mouth, ~5.9k px) from the surrounding thin line art solely by their local thickness, distinguishing them from the legitimate solid eye pupils (which are explicitly allowed and were left untouched, confirmed by visual inspection of every component found by the same opening operation). Those two regions were set to white, and the patched raster was re-traced through coloring.py's own to_bitmap/trace_paths/build_svg (imported directly, not re-invoked via the CLI) to produce the final phix174.coloring.svg. See phix174.verdicts.json for the measured final bleed numbers.
command: uv run --script .claude/skills/microbe-render/scripts/coloring.py --microbe phix174 --set bacteriophages --prompt-file <prompt v2, see attempts 1-4 in .tmp_phix174/coloring_prompt_v2.txt> --speech-en "Tiny me — my whole instruction book was the very first ever fully read!" --speech-de "Winzig, ich — mein ganzer Bauplan war der allererste, der je komplett gelesen wurde!" --model gemini-3-pro-image --attempt 2   (then deterministically patched offline; see status)
prompt:
A black-and-white CHILDREN'S COLORING BOOK page, square 1:1, 1080x1080.

THIS IS A MACRO CLOSE-UP SHOT, LIKE A ZOOMED-IN PHONE CAMERA PHOTO TAKEN TOO CLOSE. The subject is so close to the "camera" that it does NOT fully fit in the frame: the top of the little round phage character is CUT OFF by the TOP edge, and the giant round bacterium-planet character's body is CUT OFF by the LEFT edge, the RIGHT edge, AND the BOTTOM edge simultaneously — its curved body must physically touch and cross all three of those edges, filling most of the lower-left two-thirds of the canvas. There must be ZERO empty white background space visible anywhere in the image — every part of the 1080x1080 canvas is covered by either black line-art or white space that belongs INSIDE a drawn shape. If you can see plain empty background at any edge, the drawing is WRONG — redo it bigger and closer, and specifically make sure the bacterium's outline runs off the LEFT edge of the canvas, not just the right and bottom.

SCENE (draw it oversized, then let the frame crop it): The tiniest, simplest character of its family — a small, perfectly ROUND ball-shaped phage character (a plain round circle body, NOT elongated, NOT tall) with big happy cartoon eyes and a big smile, studded all around its edge with small, blunt, evenly-spaced rounded bumps (like tiny rounded rivets or gumdrops sitting flush on the ball's outline) — NOT legs, NOT spikes, NOT rays, NOT a starburst, just a cheerful polka-dot-studded round ball. THIS CHARACTER HAS NO LEGS, NO STALK, AND NO TAIL OF ANY KIND — unlike its cousins it does not stand or walk on anything; it simply floats and rests directly against things, touching them with two or three of its rounded edge-bumps. It sits in the upper-left of the frame, floating just above and touching a GIANT round smiling bacterium-planet character that fills most of the rest of the frame (standing in for E. coli, drawn as an enormous friendly circle/oval so large that only a curved portion of its outline and one cheerful face fit in frame, its edges running off the left, right and bottom of the canvas). The bacterium has a simple, plain, UNDECORATED open hatch/porthole drawn directly on its body — a plain circular doorway outline with a small round hinged door-flap swung open beside it — this hatch is a plain mechanical opening with NO face, NO eyes, and NO expression of its own; it is not a character, just a doorway. The little phage character reaches out with one small rounded edge-bump and places a single tiny rolled-up scroll (tied with a little bow, representing its whole tiny instruction book) directly into the open hatch opening. Both the phage and the bacterium (on its own single face, drawn once, kept simple) are smiling. No fight, no forcing, no bursting, no popping. Keep the background almost bare aside from two or three simple rounded sparkle-free dots near the scroll — no other objects, and absolutely no second face or second character anywhere near the hatch.

STYLE — coloring book line art: BOLD, THICK, EVEN BLACK OUTLINES on pure WHITE. Every shape fully closed. NO shading, NO grey tones, NO hatching, NO gradients, NO colour fill, NO solid black fills anywhere (eyes may have a small solid pupil only). Simple, cheerful, chunky shapes with open white space INSIDE each shape for colouring.

STRICTLY FORBIDDEN:
- Any visible empty white background, wall, sky or margin space — the artwork must be so zoomed-in and oversized that it touches or crosses every one of the four edges. The bacterium's body MUST cross the LEFT edge as well as the right and bottom edges.
- ANY starburst, radiating burst, sparkle rays, sunbeam rays, radiating speed lines, or a halo of rays anywhere — this applies especially to the small edge-bumps studding the round phage character, which must be SHORT, BLUNT and ROUNDED, sitting flush on the ball's outline, never long, never pointed, and never drawn as spikes or thin rays fanning out from a hub.
- Any legs, feet, stalk, stem or tail of any kind on the phage character.
- A tall, elongated, or capsule-shaped body for the phage character.
- A SECOND face or any separate small creature anywhere near the hatch — exactly TWO characters total.
- ANY rectangle, box outline, picture frame, panel edge, border line or vignette around the whole picture.
- NO text, letters, numbers, words, captions, labels, signatures or watermarks.
- NO speech bubble or thought bubble (added separately afterwards).
- NO fighting, no bursting/popping cell, no bite marks, no blood, no medical tools, no sick or sad character, no needles.
- NO full human figure or human face anywhere.
- The phage character never bites, stings or forces its way in — the hatch is already open and welcoming.
patch_method: morphological opening (17x17) isolating solid-black regions by local thickness, erased to white, re-traced offline with no extra API call
